name: Report risk and run stress tests (monthly risk report pack)
summary: Each month the portfolio risk team turns the month-end risk run into a report pack for each of five client portfolios and for the CIO: exposures, active risk against budget, limit use and breaches, liquidity coverage, counterparty exposure and standard stress results. In quarter-end months it also selects and runs a fuller set of stress scenarios and writes the quarterly risk report for the board and the client boards, which the chief risk officer approves. Most of the elapsed time is waiting for reconciled month-end data, inputs from the liquidity and counterparty teams and review slots; most of the effort is re-cutting the same numbers into each client's own format. Private assets modelled through proxies, data breaks and a legacy risk system replaced in 2022 are the usual sources of rework.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian provincial public-sector asset manager with about $79 billion for four client institutions and five client portfolios, with a nine-person portfolio risk team.
baseline.notes: Snapshot at the end of 2021: five client portfolios, four pools, a legacy risk system with a replacement selected in 2021 and partly live in December 2022.

trigger: Month end: the month-end positions, prices and benchmarks are loaded and the monthly reporting cycle opens.
end_state: The monthly pack has been approved and released to the CIO and client reporting; in quarter-end months the quarterly risk report has also been approved by the chief risk officer and filed for the board and client boards; any follow-up question has been answered.

volume.seasonality: Quarter-end months (March, June, September, December) add the quarterly stress testing and board report; the December pack also feeds year-end client reviews.

evidence.note: Five client portfolios plus one total fund and CIO pack each month, per the organisation file's driver; quarterly client and board risk reports described by the model manager and required at least quarterly by the insurance client policy.

systems.name: Risk analytics system (third-party factor and stress models)
Order management, pre-trade compliance and investment book of record platform (vendor software as a service)
Investment data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Market data terminals and vendor feeds (prices, indices, reference data)
Private markets investment accounting and monitoring system (commitments, calls, distributions, valuations)

steps.name: Load month-end positions, prices and benchmarks into the risk system
steps.description: After the last business day of the month the overnight feeds load end-of-day positions from the book of record, prices, exchange rates and benchmark constituents into the risk system. The month-end run reuses the daily risk batch, so nothing is touched by hand.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Risk system with factor models and stress tests described in the annual report and vendor page; the wait covers the overnight batch and month ends that fall on a weekend.

steps.name: Open the monthly cycle and roll forward the report packs
steps.description: A risk analyst opens the reporting calendar, copies last month's workbook and slide templates for each client portfolio and the total fund pack, updates dates and benchmark names and notes which month is a quarter end.

error.defect_description: A template keeps last month's date or benchmark label.

evidence.note: Common practice for template-driven monthly reporting. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Check month-end data completeness against accounting and reconciliations
steps.description: The analyst compares market values by portfolio and pool in the risk system with the reconciled book of record and the preliminary month-end accounting values, checks that private holdings carry the latest valuations rolled forward for calls and distributions, and that pooled and external fund holdings are looked through. Gaps or breaks are listed for data management.

error.defect_description: A stale private asset value or a missing look-through position is accepted.

evidence.note: Private market risks are hard to aggregate and modelled from valuations and proxies; the wait is for reconciled positions and preliminary accounting values about two business days after month end. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Correct upstream security, price or holdings data
steps.description: An investment data analyst fixes the security master record, missing or stale price, private holding mapping or look-through file named in the exception list and tells the risk analyst, who re-maps any proxy in the risk system before the rerun.

error.defect_description: A correction is applied to the wrong security or date.

evidence.note: Data management corrects reference data in the organisation file's description of its role. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Run month-end risk analytics and standard stress scenarios
steps.description: The risk system recalculates total and active risk, value at risk, factor and currency exposures and risk contributions for every client portfolio, pool and strategy, and runs the standard library of historical stress scenarios such as the 2008 crisis and March 2020.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Total, active and factor risk, historical and custom stress tests described in the annual report; overnight rerun wait is an author estimate.

steps.name: Review month-end risk results and explain changes
steps.description: The analyst compares each portfolio's risk numbers with last month, traces large moves to trades, market moves or asset mix changes, and checks that private asset proxies and leverage look sensible. Moves that cannot be explained are usually data errors and go back for correction.

error.defect_description: A risk change is explained wrongly or a mapping error is missed.

evidence.note: Risk measurement and monitoring across strategies and client portfolios described in the annual report. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Collect liquidity coverage and counterparty exposure inputs
steps.description: The analyst takes the month-end liquidity coverage results from the total portfolio team's weekly liquidity forecast and the counterparty exposure figures from investment risk oversight, checks they are for the same date, and chases either team when they are late.

error.defect_description: A liquidity or counterparty figure from a different date is used.

evidence.note: Liquidity coverage ratio and daily counterparty exposure monitoring described in the annual report; wait for other teams is an author estimate.

steps.name: Summarise limit use, breaches and policy range status for the month
steps.description: The analyst pulls the month's warnings and breaches from the daily limit log, computes month-end use of active risk budgets, leverage, currency and concentration limits and each client's policy ranges, and notes how each breach was cured or excepted.

error.defect_description: A breach cured during the month is omitted from the table.

control.basis: Board-approved investment risk limits and client statements of investment policies (The insurance client policy requires performance, risk and compliance to be reviewed at least quarterly)

evidence.note: Client policy requires at least quarterly risk and compliance review; limits and risk appetite in the risk framework. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Build the client-specific risk exhibits
steps.description: The analyst exports tables from the risk system and fills each client's own template: exposures by asset class and factor, risk contributions, limit use, liquidity coverage, counterparty exposure and standard stress results. Each client wants a different layout and level of detail, so the same numbers are re-cut and re-charted several times.

error.defect_description: A figure is pasted from the wrong date or portfolio, or a chart is not refreshed.

evidence.note: The model manager redesigned board and client risk reporting in 2021 to make it scalable as clients grow; separate client formats per the organisation file. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Reconcile the exhibits to the risk system and accounting values
steps.description: A second analyst ticks the totals in each exhibit back to the risk system export and the month-end market values and asset mix used in the client monthly report, and lists differences for the preparer to fix.

error.defect_description: A difference is missed and passes to review.

control.basis: Risk reporting procedure: four-eyes check of report figures before review

evidence.note: Common maker-checker practice for report production. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Write the risk commentary
steps.description: A senior risk manager writes a page per pack on what drove risk this month, how active risk compares with the budget, any limit events and their cure, liquidity coverage and points to watch, in the tone each client prefers.

error.defect_description: Commentary misstates a driver or omits a limit event.

evidence.note: The 2021 risk report combines detailed quantitative information with higher level commentary. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Director reviews the pack and commentary
steps.description: The director of portfolio risk reads each pack, challenges explanations of large moves and limit events, checks that wording is consistent across clients and either approves release or sends comments back to the risk manager.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Risk management framework: independent risk measurement and reporting with director sign-off before release

evidence.note: Independent risk perspective in the model manager's framework; FSRA observed a separate risk control team reporting independently. Review rates and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Publish the monthly pack to the CIO, client reporting and relationship managers
steps.description: The analyst saves the final PDF and workbook, completes the release checklist, emails the pack to the CIO and portfolio managers and sends each client's risk page to client reporting for the monthly client report, then logs the release date.

error.defect_description: The wrong client's page is sent to client reporting.

next.condition: client or CIO asks follow-up questions
quarter-end month: quarterly stress testing and board pack

evidence.note: Monthly and quarterly risk reports to clients and the board; one month in three is a quarter end. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Answer follow-up questions on the pack
steps.description: When the CIO, a relationship manager or a client's staff asks why a number moved or wants a different cut of exposures, the analyst reruns or re-cuts the analysis in the risk system and drafts a short answer.

error.defect_description: The extra cut uses a different portfolio definition from the pack.

evidence.note: Organisation file says analysts answer client questions on the reports. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Select and calibrate the quarter's stress scenarios
steps.description: The risk manager chooses the quarter's scenarios: historical events, prospective shocks such as an inflation surge, stagflation, an equity crash or a rate rise, and any client-requested scenario, sets shock sizes for each risk factor and for private asset proxies, and agrees the set with the director.

error.defect_description: A scenario is mis-specified or private asset shocks are inconsistent with public market shocks.

evidence.note: Historical and prospective single and combined shocks described by the model manager; granular scenarios as leading practice per FSRA; stress tests needed beyond value at risk per VOLTS. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Run quarterly stress tests and stressed liquidity coverage
steps.description: The analyst runs each scenario for every client portfolio, pool and the total fund, adds the liquidity coverage under stress using the liquidity team's outflow assumptions, and exports results by asset class and factor.

error.defect_description: A wrong scenario set or proxy is applied to a portfolio.

evidence.note: Stress tests and liquidity coverage under past stressed markets and a one-in-20-year event described by the model manager. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Review stress results for plausibility
steps.description: The risk manager compares stress losses with past quarters and with simple rules of thumb, checks that private asset results move consistently with public markets and asks for reruns where a result looks wrong.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Common review practice. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Build the quarterly risk insights exhibits for the board and client boards
steps.description: The analyst builds the quarterly exhibits: total fund and client risk against appetite, concentrations, limit breaches in the quarter, liquidity coverage, counterparty exposure and the stress test results, in the board template and in each client's quarterly format.

error.defect_description: An exhibit mixes month-end and quarter-end figures.

evidence.note: Quarterly Risk Insights report introduced in 2021; board reporting of exposures against limits and stress results recommended in the VOLTS review. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Draft the board risk report narrative
steps.description: The risk manager writes the narrative for the board paper: key risks and how they changed, limit events and remediation, liquidity position, what the stress tests show and any proposed limit or methodology changes.

error.defect_description: The narrative overstates or understates a risk.

evidence.note: Board risk reporting with commentary. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Director reviews the quarterly risk report
steps.description: The director reviews the exhibits and narrative for accuracy, consistency with the monthly packs and messages for the board, and returns comments to the risk manager.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Common review layer. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Chief risk officer approves the quarterly risk report
steps.description: The chief risk officer reads the board paper, may ask for an extra scenario or a change of emphasis, and approves it for the board and client board packages.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

control.basis: Board Investment Committee mandate to monitor the principal risks of investment activities, with the chief risk officer accountable for risk reporting to the board

evidence.note: The Board Investment Committee monitors principal investment risks; risk reports go to the Board. Wait is an author estimate.

steps.name: Submit the board paper and send quarterly pages to client reporting
steps.description: The analyst files the approved paper with the board secretariat by the paper deadline and sends each client's quarterly risk and stress pages to the client reporting and relationship teams for the client board reports.

error.defect_description: A superseded version is filed.

next.condition: board, CIO or client asks for an extra scenario

evidence.note: Ten board meetings in 2021 and a quarterly risk report. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Run an additional scenario requested by the CIO, board or a client
steps.description: The analyst defines and runs the extra scenario or sensitivity, such as a deeper inflation shock or a currency move, and drafts a one-page answer with the results for the portfolios concerned.

error.defect_description: The extra scenario is run on the wrong date's positions.

evidence.note: The model manager increased the number and types of stress tests in 2022. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

steps.name: Review and send the follow-up answer
steps.description: The risk manager checks the answer against the pack, edits the wording and sends it to the person who asked, copying the relationship manager when a client asked.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors in inputs pass through.

evidence.note: Common practice. Times are author estimates; no published time study of pension risk reporting was found.

exceptions.name: Month-end data gaps or breaks
exceptions.description: Unmapped securities, stale private values or missing look-through holdings are fixed by data management and the risk batch is rerun overnight.

exceptions.name: Unexplained risk change traced to data
exceptions.description: A move the analyst cannot explain turns out to be a data or mapping error and goes back for correction and rerun.

exceptions.name: Exhibit figures do not reconcile
exceptions.description: The second analyst finds a pasted figure or chart that does not agree with the risk system or accounting values.

exceptions.name: Director sends commentary back
exceptions.description: The director challenges an explanation or wording and the risk manager revises the commentary.

exceptions.name: Quarter-end stress testing and board report
exceptions.description: In quarter-end months the pack is extended with the quarter's stress scenarios and the board's quarterly risk report, reviewed by the director and approved by the chief risk officer.

exceptions.name: Follow-up question or extra scenario
exceptions.description: The CIO, the board or a client asks for an explanation or an extra scenario after release.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month end to release of the monthly pack (quarter-end packs end when the board report is filed)
benchmarks.population: Monthly risk packs of a Canadian public-sector asset manager, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author estimate: the client monthly report inserts the risk summary about 12 to 13 days after month end, so the pack is released before that; quarter-end board reports follow board paper deadlines three to six weeks after quarter end.

benchmarks.population: The insurance client insurance fund, managed by the model manager

evidence.note: Performance, risk and compliance reviewed at least quarterly.
Ten board meetings plus committee meetings in 2021.

benchmarks.unit: confidence level of annual value at risk used by peers
benchmarks.population: Canadian public pension investment managers (the national pension fund manager, AIMCo)

evidence.note: Both use 95% value at risk; the VOLTS review shows it misses non-linear tail risk.

pain_points.description: Each client wants its own report format, so the same risk numbers are re-cut, re-charted and re-checked several times; the model manager redesigned its reporting in 2021 partly to make it scalable as clients are added.
Private assets are modelled through proxies and lagged valuations and not all private market risks can be aggregated, so month-end data checks and reruns take much of the first week.

Value at risk measures understate tail and non-linear risks, so boards need stress test results reported regularly; designing plausible scenarios across public and private assets takes senior time each quarter.
The legacy risk system was being replaced (selected in 2021, partly live in December 2022), so exhibits were assembled by exporting to spreadsheets and slides by hand.
Director and chief risk officer review slots around board paper deadlines delay quarter-end reports.

evidence.note: Author estimate of a common queue.

Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

sources.supports: Toronto hourly wages for NOC 11101: low 27.97, median 41.60, high 73.57 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: Unit and volume: five client portfolio packs and one total fund and CIO pack a month (mode 6). In quarter-end months each pack is extended and the board's quarterly risk report is produced; this is modelled as a 0.33 branch per pack rather than as separate cases.

The daily risk calculation belongs to daily-risk-limit-monitoring and this process reuses its month-end run. The client-specific quarterly pages for client board meetings and the risk manager's presentation are counted in client-quarterly-reporting (its steps s07 and s26); this workflow produces the stress results and quarterly risk report those steps use, so the two do not double count.

Cycle time runs from month end to release of the monthly pack, or to filing of the quarterly board report in quarter-end months. The monthly pack is released before the client monthly report's risk section is assembled about 12 to 13 days after month end.

The model manager used a legacy third-party risk system until its replacement was implemented in 2022; BarraOne is cited only as an example of the factor, value at risk and stress capabilities such systems have, not as the model manager's vendor.

interfaces.triggered_by shares describe which input usually arrives last and releases the pack: the month-end daily risk run, the warehouse reporting data set, the weekly liquidity report, the counterparty exposure review or, rarely, a client request.
The investment data analyst takes part to correct upstream data although the process map lists only risk roles; the role exists in the organisation file.

Loaded costs come from the organisation file: Job Bank Toronto wages deflated 9% to 2021, plus variable pay, times a 1.35 loading for analysts and managers; investment professionals and executives are priced from estimated total pay.

Staffing: about 1.3 FTE in total (0.9 analyst, 0.35 senior manager). Hands-on time times volume implies a similar figure; the rest of the five analysts' and three senior managers' time goes to daily monitoring, asset mix reviews and client quarterly reports.
Times, waits and rework probabilities are author estimates (tier C) because no published time study of risk reporting at pension investment managers was found.
